subject: WBR prep · Mon 23 Nov 3 pm · Garima [WBR-20261123-garima]

facts.sku_drivers: Henna Paste - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹5.8 L); Root Touch Up Pack of 2 - QC (₹1.3 L)

questions.text: Henna on Blinkit closed at ₹27.5 L against a ₹32.0 L target (85.8%), down 23.8% on the previous week, with Henna Paste - Pack of 2 - QC accounting for −₹5.8 L. What caused the drop on that SKU, and is it recovering?

review_period_facts.sku_drivers: Henna Paste - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹2.8 L); Root Touch Up Pack of 2 - QC (₹1.1 L)

questions.answer: Garima attributes the drop to Henna Paste Pack of 2 stock-outs in west and central cities (Mumbai availability 55.0 to 12.1), says availability is recovering (Mumbai 58%, Pune 91% on 17 Nov), and says a PO bump request has been raised.
questions.why: Stock-outs fit the −₹5.8 L Pack of 2 gap, and the review period shows recovery (+6.2% WoW, attainment 92.2% vs 85.8%), but there is no date for the PO bump, the 4.2 L drop she quotes does not match the dashboard's −23.8%, and discount stays 4.1% vs 3.5% guideline (+0.6 pp) without comment.
questions.ask: When will the PO bump land, what availability do Mumbai and Pune hold by month end, and why is discount still +0.6 pp over guideline?

facts.sku_drivers: Himalayan Lavender 125g - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹2.8 L); Tomato Basil Soap 125g Pack of 2 - QC (−₹1.5 L)

questions.text: Soap on Blinkit did ₹38,555 against a ₹4.5 L target (8.6%), with Himalayan Lavender 125g - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹2.8 L) the largest shortfall. Ad spend was ₹20,948 against an ad plan showing −₹14,667, which looks like a data error, and that spend is 54.3% of sales vs 11.8% for the platform. Can you confirm the correct plan figure and explain what happened on these Pack of 2 SKUs?

review_period_facts.sku_drivers: Himalayan Lavender 125g - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹3.2 L); Tomato Basil Soap 125g Pack of 2 - QC (−₹85,248)

questions.answer: Soaps were planned to launch on 1 Nov, slipped because of Diwali, and went live on 15 Nov in a limited number of cities.
questions.why: A late launch plausibly explains ₹38,555 vs a ₹4.5 L target (8.6%), but she did not confirm the plan figure or re-plan the target, and spend is still 140% of plan and 32.6% of sales vs 9.2% for the platform in the review period.
questions.ask: What is the realistic target for the launch cities, and why is ad spend running at 140% of plan on a launch this small?

review_period_facts.sku_drivers: Henna Paste - Pack of 2 - QC (−₹1.0 L)

questions.answer: Zepto Henna Pack of 2 had a stock-out (availability 72% to 39% on 10-11 Nov), is back to 77% by 19 Nov with daily sales up 30%, and stock is being pushed to Mumbai (42%) and Chennai (9%).

questions.ask: By what date will Mumbai and Chennai be back above 70% availability, and what is the weekly revenue you expect once they are?

 Q5. Face Wash on Zepto beat target at ₹4.0 L vs ₹3.8 L, but ad spend was ₹1.7 L against a plan of ₹1.5 L, and ROAS dropped to 1.35 from 4.28 the previous week. What changed in the campaigns, and is the extra spend still paying back? 
 Ans: Ubtan ad spends increased by nearly 4×, rising from ₹35K (Nov 4–10) to ₹1.46L (Nov 11–17), while CPC also increased significantly from ₹24 to ₹69. Although Face Wash sales grew by ₹74K, from ₹2.52L to ₹3.26L, the additional ₹1.11L spent on Ubtan generated only ~₹69K in incremental sales, translating to a return of just ₹0.60 per ₹1 spent. Moreover, Ubtan was already witnessing organic growth, with weekly sales increasing from ₹1.73L in October to ₹2.22L during Nov 4–10, even at a lower ad spend of ₹35K. Given the limited incremental returns and rising acquisition costs, we will be reducing Ubtan ad spends and reallocating the budget more efficiently. Spends were shifted to display properties which have now been reduced.
